scenes.headline: How public agent skills become RL training worlds
scenes.sub: NVIDIA's Skill2Env, a compiler from SKILL.md files to containerised tasks.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cirrus! NVIDIA turned the skills people publish for agents into worlds agents train in. Here's how.

scenes.label: What collective means
scenes.text: Collective means the training distribution: tasks compiled from what thousands of practitioners wrote down, not shared replay or joint policy updates.
scenes.say: Collective means the training data itself: tasks compiled from what thousands of people wrote down.

steps.say: A public skill is a folder of written instructions. An investigator agent reads one and plans the checkable workflows it teaches.
For each workflow, it samples six axes, from difficulty to persona.

steps.note: tests and rubric are frozen before the solution exists
steps.say: A creator agent builds the world, the tests and the rubric, and only then writes the reference solution.

steps.note: 3.4k Skills became 7,971 tasks across thirteen domains
steps.say: Then two gates, with no model in them: the reference must earn full reward, and a do-nothing agent must earn zero. Otherwise, the task is dropped.
Here's the paper's drawing. Three of its six panels are model work.
The one that decides what survives is Verify, and it involves no model at all.

scenes.label: of the tasks are software engineering, in a corpus spanning thirteen domains
scenes.note: other training sets in the comparison are one or two slices wide
scenes.say: Twenty-two and a half percent is software engineering. Business, marketing, research, design and more together outweigh it.

scenes.title: The rubric run's reward
scenes.say: Then reinforcement learning. One run rewards only tests; another adds a rubric term.

parts.note: the programmatic reward from the task's tests, 0 to 1
parts.say: The first term is the tests' reward, from zero to one.

parts.note: a judge's score for the trace, -5 to 5, given the rubric
parts.say: S is a judge's score for the trace, from minus five to five, reading the rubric.

parts.note: so the judge moves the reward by at most 0.2
parts.say: So the judge can move the reward by at most point two.

scenes.title: Preferred over the base model by a Skill-holding judge
scenes.note: outcome-only wins every benchmark; the rubric run gives back 4.0 on Terminal-Bench
scenes.say: Outcome-only wins every benchmark. But a judge holding the skill prefers the rubric run's work seventy-three percent of the time, against fifty-four and a half.

scenes.text: Collective preference and benchmark pass rate are two objectives; right now we can only optimise one at a time.

recap: Skills compile into tested, rubric-graded RL tasks
Two model-free gates: Oracle passes, no-op fails
The rubric buys method and costs benchmark points
scenes.say: To recap: skills become tasks, two model-free gates, and a rubric that trades benchmark points for method.
